summary: Defines the technology-specific information needed when GMPLS signaling is used for SONET and SDH. It also provides minor clarification to RFC 3946. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: Optical telephone networks have fixed-size channels. This explains how a signaling system asks for the right-size channel.

subtitle: How GMPLS signaling asks for SONET and SDH circuits: the traffic parameters and the SUKLM label.

tldr.problem: GMPLS signaling is generic, but SONET and SDH networks have their own fixed signal sizes, concatenation rules and overhead, so a request needs technology-specific fields.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a set of SONET/SDH traffic parameters (signal type, concatenation, multiplier, transparency, profile) carried in RSVP-TE and CR-LDP objects, plus a 32-bit SUKLM label that names an exact time-slot in the multiplex.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 3946 with minor clarifications and is a Proposed Standard that was later updated by RFC 6344.

today: RFC 4606 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 3946 and was later updated by RFC 6344. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Where This Document Fits
sections.content:
Generalized MPLS (GMPLS) extends MPLS beyond packet switching to four more classes of interface: Layer-2 Switch Capable, Time-Division Multiplex (TDM), Lambda Switch Capable and Fiber-Switch Capable. RFC 3471 gives the functional description of the signaling, RFC 3473 the RSVP-TE formats and RFC 3472 the CR-LDP formats.

This RFC supplies the details specific to SONET (Synchronous Optical Network) and SDH (Synchronous Digital Hierarchy). Per RFC 3471, those details travel in traffic-parameter objects. The abstract notes that the document also provides minor clarification to RFC 3946, which it obsoletes.
sections.plainLanguage: GMPLS is a general way to book network paths. This document adds the special words you need when the path is a SONET or SDH optical line.

sections.title: The SONET/SDH Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
The traffic parameters describe the signal being requested. They are seven fields: Signal Type (8 bits), RCC (8 bits), NCC (16 bits), NVC (16 bits), Multiplier (16 bits), Transparency (32 bits) and Profile (32 bits).

The Signal Type names an Elementary Signal. Transforms are then applied to it in a strict order: contiguous concatenation (RCC and NCC), virtual concatenation (NVC), transparency, and finally a multiplication (MT). A zero in any transform means it is not applied, except that MT cannot be zero and is ignored when it equals one.

These parameters MUST be used when the label is encoded as SUKLM and when requesting a Section/RS or Line/MS overhead transparent signal. A fully transparent signal instead uses the parameters and label encoding of RFC 3471, Section 3.2.
sections.plainLanguage: You pick a basic building block, then optionally glue several together, stack copies, or ask that the wrapping be left untouched. The steps must be done in the same order every time.

sections.title: Concatenation, Multiplier, Transparency and Profile
sections.content:
Contiguous concatenation is requested with RCC, a vector of flags where only flag 1 (standard contiguous concatenation, the low-order bit) is defined. NCC gives the number of identical components to concatenate. An upstream node can set several RCC flags to offer a choice; the downstream node picks one, or MUST refuse the request if it supports none. When a SONET STS-Nc SPE with N=3*X is requested, the signal type must be STS-3c SPE and NCC must equal X, to ease SONET and SDH interworking.

Virtual concatenation is requested with NVC, the number of same-type signals to be virtually concatenated; 0 means none. The Multiplier says how many identical signals form the final signal. It defaults to one and zero is invalid: a node that receives zero MUST generate a PathErr or NOTIFICATION message.

Transparency says which overhead fields must reach the far end unmodified. Flag 1 is Section/Regenerator Section layer and flag 2 is Line/Multiplex Section layer. Section layer transparency means whole frames are delivered unmodified, so pointers cannot be adjusted. Transparency is only applicable to the STS-1/STM-0 and larger frame signal types. The Profile field is for capabilities such as monitoring; no standard profile is defined, so it SHOULD be zero when sent and ignored when received.
sections.plainLanguage: You can ask for one big pipe made of touching pieces, or several pieces tied together, or several copies. You can also say that the label on the outside of the parcel must not be changed on the way.

sections.title: RSVP-TE and CR-LDP Encodings
sections.content:
In RSVP-TE the parameters travel in the SONET/SDH SENDER_TSPEC object (Class = 12, C-Type = 4) and the FLOWSPEC object (Class = 9, C-Type = 4). The format is the same for both. The FLOWSPEC received in a Resv message SHOULD be identical to the SENDER_TSPEC received in the matching Path message; otherwise a ResvErr with "Traffic Control Error/Bad Flowspec value" SHOULD be generated. There is no Adspec for the SONET/SDH SENDER_TSPEC.

In CR-LDP they travel in the SONET/SDH Traffic Parameters TLV, whose type field is 0x0838.

Intermediate and egress nodes MUST check that they and the chosen interfaces can support the requested Signal Type, RCC, NCC, NVC and Multiplier. In RSVP-TE a failure produces a PathErr with "Traffic Control Error/Service unsupported"; in CR-LDP it produces a NOTIFICATION with a "Resource Unavailable" status code. Intermediate nodes MUST also check transparency in the same way.
sections.plainLanguage: The order form is stuffed into the envelope used by the signaling system. If a station along the way cannot supply what is asked, it sends back a note saying so.

sections.title: SONET and SDH Labels (SUKLM)
sections.content:
SONET and SDH each define a multiplexing structure that is a tree. A label names the exact position, meaning the first time-slot, of a signal in that tree. It is carried in the Generalized Label (Class-Num = 16, C-Type = 2, or TLV 0x0825) as a 32-bit value made of five fields: S (16 bits), then U, K, L and M (4 bits each). This extends the (K, L, M) numbering of G.707. Numbering starts at 1 and zero means not significant.

  • S indexes an STS-3/AUG-1 inside an STS-N/STM-N.
  • U (1 to 3) indexes an STS-1 SPE/VC-3 inside it.
  • K (1 to 3) indexes a TUG-3 inside a VC-4.
  • L (1 to 7) indexes a VT Group/TUG-2.
  • M indexes the VT or VC inside it: 1 to 2 for VT3 (SONET only), 3 to 5 for VT2/VC-12 and 6 to 9 for VT1.5/VC-11.

For contiguous concatenation a single label gives the lowest time-slot. For virtual concatenation and multiplication, an ordered list of labels is given, which keeps the components on a single link. A label is context sensitive: it can only be read together with the traffic parameters. SUKLM MUST be used for any request that is not transparent.
sections.plainLanguage: A label is like a seat number built from section, row and seat. Each number narrows down where in the optical stream your signal sits.

sections.title: Appendix and Annex Examples
sections.content:
Appendix 1 adds one optional signal type, value 20, "VC-3 via AU-3 at the end". It tells the last hops that a VC-3 must end in the AU-3 branch, which a router needs if it wants to demultiplex the VC-3 into lower-order LSPs. It does not require the VC-3 to use the AU-3 branch anywhere else.

Annex 1 shows how real signals map to the fields. A VC-4-16c is signal type 6 with RCC 1, NCC 16, NVC 0 and MT 1. A VC-4-7v is signal type 6 with NVC 7. An STM-16 with Multiplex Section layer transparency is signal type 10 with T set to 2. A 3 x STS-768c SPE is signal type 6 with RCC 1, NCC 256 and MT 3.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples are filled-in order forms, so you can see how a big pipe, a bundle of small ones and a left-alone parcel are each written down.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC introduces no new security considerations beyond RFC 3473 and RFC 3472. GMPLS security is described in Section 11 of RFC 3471, which refers to RFC 3209 for RSVP-TE and RFC 3212 for CR-LDP.

For IANA, the three values assigned for RFC 3946 now apply to this document: the two RSVP C-Types (Class 12 and Class 9, both C-Type 4) and the LDP TLV type for the SONET/SDH Traffic Parameters TLV.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to lock down here. The safety rules come from the documents this one builds on.

fields.name: Signal Type
fields.desc: Elementary Signal that forms the requested LSP.

fields.name: Multiplier
fields.desc: Number of identical signals; default one.

fields.name: Profile
fields.desc: Reserved for capabilities such as monitoring.

items.label: STS-3c SPE / VC-4
items.desc: Dedicated type to ease SONET and SDH interworking.

fields.name: S
fields.desc: Index of an STS-3/AUG-1 inside the STS-N/STM-N.

fields.name: U
fields.desc: Index of an STS-1 SPE/VC-3 within it.

fields.name: K
fields.desc: Index of a TUG-3 within a VC-4.

fields.name: M
fields.desc: Index of a VT or VC inside the group.
